title: Montclair Health - Private deployment infra guardrails & KMS onboarding
summary: Deep dive on private/VPC deployment security posture. Covered network isolation patterns, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, SOC2 evidence mapping, RBAC and SSO integration, KMS key management options and data residency considerations. Agreed to run a connectivity lab, provide KMS integration doc, and share SOC2/ISO artifacts. Customer to provide list of allowed egress endpoints and pilot infra account details.
topics: network isolation patterns (VPC peering vs private link)
ingress load balancing and ingress security
egress restrictions, proxying, and firewall rules
encryption at rest/transport and KMS/HSM options
RBAC, SSO (SAML/SCIM) mapping and audit logging
SOC 2 artifact requests and ISO mapping
data residency and air-gapped on-prem options
action_items: Priya Nair: Draft KMS integration runbook + diagram (due 2025-07-16)
Jordan Lee: Share SOC2 report redacted PDF and ISO checklist link (due 2025-07-11)
Samir Patel (Montclair): Provide egress allowlist and pilot VPC CIDRs (due 2025-07-14)
Maria Lopez (Montclair): Confirm encryption key ownership requirements and HSM need (due 2025-07-18)
next_steps: Schedule 1:1 connectivity lab between Priya and Samir (Jordan to set up)
Customer to validate whether keys must be customer-managed HSM vs Redwood KMS
Run short perf test on private pilot to validate latency impact of in-VPC encryption
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're going to cover the private deployment security architecture for Montclair. I'll hand it to Priya for the deep dive.
[00:15] Priya (SE): Great, hi all. Quick agenda: network isolation, ingress/egress, firewalling, KMS and audit logs, then Q&A. We'll keep it practical.
[00:30] Alex (CTO): Sounds good. High level — our constraint is that patient PII stays in-region and we need customer-managed keys if possible. Also SOC2 artifact request.
[00:45] Maria (InfoSec): And we need RBAC integration with our SSO. We prefer SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[01:05] Priya: Totally. Redwood Private supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync; mapping roles to RBAC can be done via attribute mapping. We usually recommend least privilege service roles for inference vs admin.
[01:30] Samir (Infra): Quick question — how does the control plane talk to the private deployment? Is there a public egress or private link?
[01:45] Jordan: Good point. For Private we offer two models: managed control plane with connector over a customer-controlled egress (mTLS), or fully air-gapped on-prem with offline artifacts. For VPCs we support PrivateLink and peered VPCs depending on your network posture.
[02:10] Priya: To add, most customers do a one-way egress to Redwood endpoints over mTLS using a dedicated egress proxy; that keeps inbound from Redwood to customer infra blocked.
[02:30] Maria: We can't allow open egress to arbitrary domains; we need allowlist only. Does Redwood support static IPs for egress?
[02:45] Priya: Yes, Dedicated deployments can be provisioned with a fixed set of egress IPs, or you can route via customer NAT/proxy; we have documentation but will provide a hardened diagram.
[03:05] Speaker 6: Is there support for private link?
[03:15] Priya: Yep, AWS PrivateLink is supported for the control plane to data plane handshake; it avoids public internet entirely. For on-prem we use a connector that initiates outbound TLS to the control plane — it's an outbound-only connection.
[03:35] Alex: For KMS, our security team prefers key ownership; we need to know if Redwood can use our KMS keys, or must Redwood manage keys.
[03:50] Priya: We support customer-managed keys in two ways: a cloud KMS owner-supplied key with KMS grants, or HSM-backed keys for stricter controls. When customer-managed keys are used, Redwood never persists plaintext and keys are never exported. 
[04:10] Jordan: Also note operationally there's a latency tradeoff if each call locks/unlocks with the HSM; we typically cache derived data to avoid per-request HSM roundtrips but we can detail the options.
[04:35] Maria: We need an explicit statement about key rotation and audit logs for KMS operations.
[04:45] Priya: We'll include rotation policies and CloudTrail-equivalent audit trails in the runbook. Cloud providers' KMS generate logs; we provide hooks to ingest those for evidence.
[05:05] Samir: On network isolation: we want to avoid any inbound from Redwood. If PrivateLink is used for control signals, is there any callback that requires inbound?
[05:20] Priya: No inbound required — the dataplane connector maintains an outbound control channel. Model updates and metrics stream over that channel. In emergencies we have a signed artifact exchange workflow for manual bootstrap.
[05:40] Alex: Regarding firewalling, do you support layer 7 filtering or is it just CIDR/NACLs?
[05:55] Priya: We recommend layered controls: NACLs/CIDR for coarse restrict, stateful firewall for allowed ports, and a sidecar proxy (Envoy) if you need application-layer allowlist and mTLS between services.
[06:20] Maria: So Envoy can be used to enforce mutual TLS and token inspection?
[06:30] Priya: Exactly. The sidecar validates tokens, injects tracing headers, and enforces route-level RBAC.
[06:45] Jordan: From a compliance mapping perspective, we can map network controls to SOC2 CC6.2 and logging to CC7.x. We'll share our evidence pack.
[07:05] Lina (Compliance): On data residency: can we pin workloads to a specific region and prevent cross-region failover?
[07:20] Priya: Yes — deployment pins are supported. Automatic cross-region failover is opt-in; for your case we recommend manual failover with a strict replication plan to satisfy residency.
[07:40] Alex: How about audit logs — we need immutable logs for admins and for inference requests tied to token IDs.
[07:55] Priya: We emit detailed audit events: authorization decisions, key operations, model deploys, and per-request metadata (redacted if needed). Events can be pushed to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or delivered via syslog; retention is configurable.
[08:20] Samir: What about log enrichment with user IDs via SCIM?
[08:30] Priya: Yes, SCIM synchronizes user attributes and we include user id/email in the audit events as an identifier field.
[08:45] Maria: We need guaranteed retention periods per HIPAA-like policy; can Redwood guarantee retention windows for audit logs we push to you?
[08:58] Jordan: We don't retain customer push logs beyond the configured retention; if you push to your collector it's under your control. For stored logs in Redwood, retention is configurable and contractually bound under Dedicated/Private SLAs.
[09:20] Alex: Let's talk about ingress, specifically model endpoints. Do we expose a load balancer inside the VPC?
[09:35] Priya: Model endpoints run on customer subnets; you can front them with an internal ALB or NLB. We advise using internal ALB with security groups limiting source to your app subnets.
[09:55] Samir: Any recommendation around TLS termination? We prefer end-to-end TLS to the container.
[10:05] Priya: End-to-end is supported. Termination at the ALB is common, but you can use mutual TLS all the way to the service with client certs provisioned by your PKI.
[10:25] Speaker 6: Do you support hardware attestation for the nodes?
[10:35] Priya: For on-prem we can integrate with TPM-based attestation and Alo for cloud we rely on instance metadata attestation; we can provide options depending on your level of assurance.
[10:55] Maria: For SOC2 evidence we'll need a process doc for key lifecycle, user onboarding/offboarding, and change management.
[11:10] Jordan: We'll share a redacted SOC2 and the change mgmt runbook. We'll also map the controls to your ISO checklist.
[11:25] Alex: On the topic of egress, our security team wants egress to be via a corporate proxy to inspect traffic. Can you route through our proxy?
[11:40] Priya: Yes, you can force egress through your proxy; we support HTTP CONNECT or explicit proxy configurations. We recommend mutual TLS between the connector and proxy for authentication.
[12:00] Samir: Will that impact token streaming / performance for long-lived streams?
[12:12] Priya: There's minimal impact; we've seen a small added latency around 30–70ms depending on proxy, but throughput is generally not affected. We'll include perf numbers in the runbook.
[12:30] Maria: About RBAC — can we create role hierarchies so Data Science can call inference but not see audit logs?
[12:45] Priya: Yes, RBAC is role-based with policies scoped per model/route. Admin roles get audit access; inference-only roles can be restricted to calls and telemetry limited to operational metrics.
[13:05] Jordan: One nuance: operator-level traces occasionally include user identifiers for debugging; we can redact those by default but allow controlled unredaction with approvals.
[13:25] Alex: Great. For encryption at rest, do you encrypt model weights on disks?
[13:35] Priya: Yes, we encrypt volumes at rest using vendor KMS, and with customer-managed keys we use envelope encryption where the data encryption key (DEK) is wrapped by your CMK.
[13:55] Samir: Is there a per-tenant key? We want a key-per-customer separation.
[14:04] Priya: You can request per-customer CMKs; that's standard for Dedicated/Private.
[14:20] Lina: For on-prem air-gapped, how do model updates arrive? We can't allow outbound downloads.
[14:35] Priya: In air-gapped mode we provide signed model packages that you import manually; updates are delivered as signed artifacts and you run a validation step.
[14:50] Alex: Are model artifacts hashed and signed?
[14:58] Priya: Yes SHA256 hashes and an RSA signature; we maintain a notarized chain.
[15:10] Speaker 6: Can we do pen tests on the deployment?
[15:18] Jordan: Yes — customers can run pen tests under a coordinated schedule; we require a quick OOO and scope to avoid false alarms on monitoring. We'll share the pen test playbook.
[15:35] Maria: For incident response, do you expose forensic artifacts and snapshots?
[15:45] Priya: We can provide EBS snapshots or equivalent and export audit trails for the timeframe; access is controlled and auditable.
[15:58] Samir: How is secret rotation handled for service tokens in the cluster?
[16:08] Priya: We recommend short-lived tokens and a control plane-driven rotation workflow; tokens are stored in memory only and rotated automatically.
[16:25] Alex: We need to understand the expected failure modes for KMS — what happens if a KMS region is down?
[16:35] Priya: If using customer-managed keys in a single region, decrypt operations will fail; we advise a replicate approach with cross-region CMKs if automatic failover is required. For strict residency, manual failover is the safer option.
[16:55] Jordan: We'll include scenario matrices in the runbook enumerating failover behavior and SLO impact.
[17:10] Maria: One ask — can you provide sample audit entries for a model deployment and a decrypt operation so our auditors can validate?
[17:25] Priya: Yes we'll include sample logs with redaction markers.
[17:40] Speaker 6: Any thoughts on regulatory compliance beyond SOC2/ISO — HIPAA?
[17:52] Jordan: We have customers using Redwood for HIPAA workloads under Private with BAAs; we can share the process and controls.
[18:05] Alex: For the connector, what are the memory/CPU requirements?
[18:15] Priya: The connector is lightweight: default CPU 1vCPU and 512MB recommended for control channel, but data plane nodes need GPU or CPU depending on model. We'll send a sizing guide.
[18:35] Samir: Regarding firewall rules: what TCP/UDP ports do we need to open?
[18:45] Priya: Primarily outbound TCP 443 for control plane, several ephemeral ports for metrics and admin if using NLBs; we'll provide a precise list.
[19:00] Maria: What is the threat model for supply chain attacks on models?
[19:10] Priya: We sign artifacts, validate hashes, and maintain provenance metadata. For extra assurance you can run model verification suites before deployment.
[19:28] Jordan: We'll share the model provenance doc and the verification checklist.
[19:40] Alex: Can we have customer-managed attestations on model boot?
[19:50] Priya: For on-prem, yes via TPM attestation and signed boot chains; for cloud, instance identity documents can be used.
[20:05] Speaker 6: How does Redwood handle secrets for third-party connectors?
[20:15] Priya: They are stored encrypted with the chosen KMS and scoped per-connector; access is controlled by RBAC.
[20:30] Maria: We need to see the exact IAM roles Redwood requires in our account.
[20:40] Jordan: We'll supply a least-privilege IAM template and a checklist for role creation.
[20:55] Samir: Any audit around software supply updates for the runtime/kernel?
[21:05] Priya: We maintain signed release artifacts and CVE tracking; major kernel changes are coordinated with a maintenance window.
[21:20] Alex: Ok, let's talk timeline — we want a pilot in the next 6 weeks. What do you need from us?
[21:30] Jordan: The pilot needs a pilot VPC with two subnets, egress allowlist, and a pilot service account with SCIM user sync enabled. Samir, you'll provide CIDRs.
[21:45] Samir: We'll send that.
[21:55] Lina: For audit purposes, can Redwood produce a schedule of when data is deleted from caches?
[22:05] Priya: Yes, TTLs are configurable per-route; default is 0 for sensitive routes. We'll document cache lifecycles.
[22:20] Maria: Is KV cache encrypted?
[22:28] Priya: Yes encrypted at rest and only kept in memory for active inference; persistent caches are wrapped with DEKs.
[22:45] Speaker 6: What about model explainability telemetry — is that considered sensitive?
[22:55] Priya: Telemetry can include prompts and outputs which are sensitive; we treat them as PII-equivalent and recommend redaction and retention policies.
[23:15] Jordan: We're approaching the middle of the call — any blockers?
[23:22] Alex: KMS key ownership and the egress allowlist are main blockers.
[23:30] Priya: We'll prioritize the KMS runbook and egress examples.
[23:40] Jordan: Quick demo idea: Priya can run a connectivity lab against Samir's sandbox next week.
[23:50] Samir: Works for me.
[24:00] Priya: We'll show PrivateLink handshake, a sample KMS encrypt/decrypt with your CMK, and an audit log export.
[24:18] Maria: That would be helpful.
[24:30] Alex: On legal — we'll need a BAA and some redlines around data processing addendum.
[24:42] Jordan: Legal will follow up; I'll loop in our contracts lead after this call.
[24:55] Lina: For ISO mapping, can you provide control mappings?
[25:05] Jordan: Yes, we map to ISO clauses and can give a gap list.
[25:18] Alex: Anything we should avoid in pilot?
[25:27] Priya: Avoid multi-region replication for the pilot if residency is a blocker; keep pilot region-bound.
[25:40] Speaker 6: How do you handle token revocation if a user is offboarded mid-request?
[25:50] Priya: Tokens are short-lived; revocation is immediate for new requests and we provide a grace termination for long-running streams.
[26:05] Maria: Could you show an example of RBAC policy?
[26:12] Priya: We'll attach sample policies in the runbook.
[26:25] Jordan: Let's cover monitoring and alerting — what alerts are available out of the box?
[26:35] Priya: Alerts on failed decrypts, unauthorized access attempts, high error rates, and unusual traffic egress. We also provide tracing hooks for jaeger/zipkin.
[26:50] Samir: Do you support SIEM integration?
[26:58] Priya: Yes, logs can be shipped to Splunk, Sumo, or your in-house SIEM.
[27:10] Alex: A couple more quick things: can we disable model telemetry for certain routes?
[27:20] Priya: Yes, telemetry can be disabled per-route; we do recommend minimal operational telemetry for SLOs but that's configurable.
[27:35] Maria: For the SOC2 artifacts you'll share, will they include the test procedures?
[27:45] Jordan: We'll provide the report and a high-level description of test procedures; full details are restricted but we can provide attestation summaries.
[28:00] Priya: We're also going to provide an architecture diagram showing private link, egress proxy, ALB, and KMS flows.
[28:12] Samir: Nice.
[28:25] Alex: Let's align on dates. Jordan, you said KMS runbook due 7/16?
[28:32] Jordan: Yes.
[28:40] Maria: We'll aim to get egress allowlist to you by 7/14.
[28:48] Jordan: Perfect.
[28:55] Speaker 6: One last question — do you have a dedicated SOC engineer as a point of contact?
[29:04] Jordan: Yes, I'll introduce you to our security contact, Tina Park, in the follow-up.
[29:15] Priya: Any other technical nitty-gritty?
[29:20] Samir: For the connectivity lab, do you need RBAC accounts created beforehand?
[29:28] Priya: Just a service account and one test user; SCIM provisioning helps but we can create ephemeral creds.
[29:40] Alex: Great. If no more questions, let's recap.
[29:48] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to share SOC2/ISO artifacts, Priya to deliver KMS runbook and diagrams, Samir to send CIDRs and egress allowlist, schedule connectivity lab next week.
[30:05] Maria: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[30:12] Priya: Thanks — we'll follow up with links (security pack, runbook, IAM templates).
[30:20] Jordan: End of recording.
[52:00] [end of meeting]
